The Shepherd datafiles aren't difficult to process. I'm happy to help guide someone thru them if they're trying to implement something in Wattsi.

It occurs to me that HTML's source doesn't have any precedent for autolinking without a tag delimiter. That is, we always wrap in at least ``. If we could reduce that to `` I would be extremely happy, and I know we have that planned. But I am not sure that we need an extra Wattsi step just to allow `'color'` instead of `'color'`, especially given the potential false-positives (e.g. I presume `'x'`, `'td'`, and `'src'` from the above list are not supposed to be CSS linked) and the continuing issue of which is the best CSS spec for defining a property (see e.g. https://github.com/tabatkins/bikeshed/issues/622). In other words, I'd be OK with just finishing up this PR instead of tooling out Wattsi.

My other concern with tooling out Wattsi is that unlike Bikeshed, Wattsi doesn't have an independent concept of "specs database" that updates independently from either the tool or the input source.

We'd have to either introduce that to Wattsi directly, or maintain our own database (presumably Shepherd-derived) in the whatwg/html or whatwg/html-build repo that Wattsi uses, or something else entirely.
Added more commits. This now glosses every property I could find, and some (albeit not all) values+units+datatypes.

I'm not sure we should xref property values. Whenever a value is mentioned, the property is, too, so there's less value in xreffing the value. Plus there are lots of values that have different meaning for different properties, and some might have the same name as a property, and so on. So I think I prefer leaving values alone.

$ grep -Eo "<[a-z-]+(>|>)" source | sort | uniq -d

So, while I agree in general it doesn't seem strictly necessary to link every single value keyword (which is why I only linked 3 values rather than all of them), here's my rationale for the 3 values in question: - 'ruby-base' (of the 'display' property) - Literally the only reference to CSSRUBY in the HTML spec is in relation to 'ruby-base' - `

For the purposes of the CSS ruby model, runs of children of ruby elements that are not rt or rp elements are expected to be wrapped in anonymous boxes whose 'display' property has the value 'ruby-base'.

` - 'inline-block' (of the 'display' property) - This is linked in relation to the term "'inline-block' box" that appears in the spec several times. - CSS defines the terms "block box" & "inline box", which are already glossed. Not glossing "'inline-block' box" in some way seems inconsistent. - None of the existing references to "'inline-block' box" clarify that 'display' is the relevant property. - 'table-cell' (of the 'display' property) - Similar to 'inline-block', [the section that mentions 'table-cell'](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-dialog-element:margin-box-10) doesn't mention the 'display' property
